summary: The bill requires the Bureau of Indian Affairs to review and approve residential, business, and land mortgage packages plus right-of-way documents on Indian land within fixed deadlines of 10 to 30 days, issue delay notices, deliver title reports directly to lenders and agencies, grant tribes and federal agencies read-only access to the TAAMS land system, and create a Realty Ombudsman to enforce compliance.

scores.thoughts: The bill mandates new deadlines and procedures for BIA mortgage processing, creates a Realty Ombudsman position within the Bureau, requires annual reports to Congress, and directs a GAO study on digitization. These requirements would likely necessitate some additional administrative resources or staffing at BIA, representing a minor expansion of government operations and spending, though no new appropriations are explicitly authorized.
